title: Chapter 5 Quiz: Components
description: Test your knowledge of component creation, props, events, slots, and best practices.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main benefit of component‑based architecture?
questions.explanation: Components promote reusability and separation of concerns, making code easier to maintain and scale.

questions.question: A component can have its own `data`, `methods`, `computed`, and `watch` options.
questions.explanation: Yes, components are self‑contained units that can have their own state and logic.

questions.question: How do you register a component globally?
questions.explanation: `app.component(name, definition)` registers a component globally, making it available everywhere in the app.

questions.question: The special attribute that allows a parent to pass data to a child is called a __________.
questions.explanation: Props are used for parent → child data flow.

questions.question: A child component should directly modify the value of a prop it receives.
questions.explanation: Props are read‑only. To communicate changes, the child should emit an event and let the parent update the prop.

questions.question: Which method is used in a child component to send data to its parent?
questions.explanation: `this.$emit(eventName, payload)` triggers a custom event that the parent can listen to.

questions.question: To make a component accept arbitrary HTML content from its parent, you use __________.
questions.explanation: Slots allow the parent to inject content into the child's template.

questions.question: Named slots require the `v-slot` directive or its shorthand `#`.
questions.explanation: Yes, named slots are specified with `v-slot:name` or `#name`.

questions.question: What is the recommended naming convention for component files in a Vue project?
questions.explanation: PascalCase (e.g., `MyComponent.vue`) is the standard for single‑file components.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to define a prop with validation?
options: props: { age: { type: Number, required: true } }
questions.explanation: All are valid: simple array, simple object with type, or object with validation options.

questions.question: Global components are lazy‑loaded by default.
questions.explanation: Global components are loaded upfront. For code splitting, use local registration or async components.

questions.question: The shorthand for `v-slot:header` is __________.
questions.explanation: `#header` is the shorthand for `v-slot:header`.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `props` option in a component?
options: To define the component's local state
To list the attributes the component expects from its parent
questions.explanation: Props define the data interface the component expects from its parent.

questions.question: A component's template must have a single root element.
questions.explanation: In Vue 2, templates require a single root element. Vue 3 supports multiple root nodes (fragments).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using components?
questions.explanation: Components don't automatically improve performance; they help structure code for maintainability, but performance depends on implementation.

questions.question: The __________ option allows a component to accept a function that returns the initial data.
questions.explanation: `data` must be a function that returns an object to ensure each component instance gets its own state.

questions.question: You can use `v-model` on a custom component.
questions.explanation: Yes, `v-model` on a component is syntactic sugar for binding `modelValue` prop and listening to `update:modelValue` event.

questions.question: What is prop drilling?
options: Passing props through many levels of components
Using props to drill holes in the DOM
A technique to optimize prop updates
questions.explanation: Prop drilling occurs when you pass data down through multiple intermediate components that don't need it, just to reach a deeper child.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to define a component locally?
questions.explanation: In the Options API, you define a `components` object with the component names as keys and their definitions as values.

questions.question: Slots can have default content that appears if no content is provided.
questions.explanation: Yes, you can put content inside the `<slot>` tag; that content will be used if the parent doesn't provide any.
